Subject: Routing policy exception request — Acme HealthTech (EU-only, no-fallback)

Team,

Acme HealthTech (procurement) has formally requested a routing exception as part of their contract: they require EU-only routing and a strict "no-fallback" policy so that requests from their app never route to non-EU regions or alternate model variants. They also want a forced model selection (a particular quantized variant we've certified) for consistency across responses.

Attached: routing-exception-redline.docx (redline from Acme legal).

Questions for the group:
- Is a hard no-fallback + region lock technically supportable without a Dedicated capacity commitment?
- What are the SLO/latency/cost implications if we enforce a single model variant and disable fallback/autoscaling to fallback tiers?
- What audit controls do we need to demonstrate to Acme (logs, KMS, retention)?

Acme is pushing this as a gating requirement for signature; Rishi says procurement wants an answer before next Monday (11/10). I want product position and a clear implementation ask we can present to sales/legal.

Thanks,
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Director, Product Management
Redwood Inference

--

Subject: Re: Routing policy exception request — Acme HealthTech (EU-only, no-fallback)

Lauren — thanks for the heads up. A few clarifying points from product: 

1) By 'no-fallback' do we mean: a) disable automated fallback to cheaper/latency-tuned model variants entirely, or b) allow fallback within the same EU region but not cross-region?
2) Is the forced model variant immutable per request OR per-tenant configuration?
3) Does Acme expect us to absorb higher error/latency risk if their chosen variant is overloaded?

Initial thoughts: forcing a specific model+region is feasible as a routing policy flag (we already have per-tenant routing overrides in the console), but disabling fallback globally changes our SLO behavior and will need gating in the runtime. We should consider requiring a Dedicated capacity/SLA for customers who insist on no-fallback.

Markus/Evelyn — can you comment on engineering/security impacts? Rishi, please paste the Acme procurement language if available.

- Dev

--
Quick reply preferred; I can host a sync Wed if helpful.

Subject: Re: Routing policy exception request — Acme HealthTech (EU-only, no-fallback)

Quick technical update:

- Forced model selection: we can add a routing flag that pins a tenant to a model_id variant (e.g., "redwood-7b-eu-q4") at the API/router level. That part is straightforward and low-risk.
- Region lock: also doable by validating region attribute on request tokens and failing on mismatch. Needs work in the auth/router layer but no server-side data residency changes.
- No-fallback: this is the tricky one. Our current smart routing automatically falls back to compatible models when capacity is constrained or when quantization incompatibilities are detected. Turning that off will require us to:
  1) Add a per-tenant enforcement path that bypasses fallback logic.
  2) Add capacity reservation or reject requests when the pinned model is unavailable. Rejecting increases 5xx and client-visible errors.

Performance/ops consequences:
- p99 and error rate could spike during transient load without fallback.
- We'll need capacity-estimates.csv (attached) from Infra to size EU pools for the pinned variant.
- Short-term mitigation: require Dedicated/reserved capacity if they want no-fallback; otherwise offer a SLA-backed canary window with manual override.

Estimate: 2 sprints (4 weeks) to ship the routing flag + guardrails, + infra provisioning lead time. If legal needs guaranteed availability, we need an Annual Reserved commit or Dedicated contract.

Attachment: capacity-estimates.csv (stub)

- Markus

Subject: Re: Routing policy exception request — Acme HealthTech (EU-only, no-fallback)

Security/compliance perspective:

- Region lock + forced model selection is acceptable from a data residency point of view only if we guarantee no cross-region failover or storage of transient artifacts outside EU. We need to ensure the control plane never triggers a non-EU execution path.
- Auditability: Acme will need tamper-evident logs showing routing decisions, model_id used per request, and KMS key IDs used for any encrypted payloads. We should offer a 90-day audit log export as part of the exception.
- Risk: Hard no-fallback increases customer-facing error rates; we must ensure the customer understands and signs off on the operational risk. Legal will want explicit language.

Action items for me: I will draft the required audit controls and add them to the redline. If we move forward, require a pre-production canary (2 weeks) and an acceptance sign-off by our compliance team before GA.

- Evelyn

Adding Acme contacts so they have visibility. Procurement attached their request; legal has redlined it and sent the PDF (attached). High-level customer asks: EU-only execution, a specific model pin to ensure consistent clinical phrasing, and no automatic fallbacks that could route to faster-but-different variants. They see this as a privacy + quality requirement for production.

From Acme (short): "We cannot accept any serving path that could route requests outside the EU or to model variants that alter clinical phrasing. We require explicit audit logs and a fail-safe that rejects execution rather than routing elsewhere."

Acme's ask is contractual; they have a security questionnaire and will escalate if we can't offer it. That said, they are willing to sign a Dedicated capacity/Reserved commit if Redwood can commit to the configuration.

Attached: Acme_no_fallback_routing_req.pdf (pdf)

Timeline: Procurement asks for a written engineering position by 11/10 so they can align legal and exec. My ask: can product/engineering give a decision and a proposed path (Dedicated vs hosted with limitations) by COB 11/10?

- Rishi

Thanks everyone — summary and proposed decision for sales/legal:

1) Product position: We will support a per-tenant routing flag that enforces region-lock and pins a specific model_id.
2) No-fallback policy: Allowed only with an explicit capacity commitment (Dedicated or Reserved annual commit). Without a capacity commitment we cannot guarantee availability and will not offer a hard no-fallback.
3) Security controls: Provide tamper-evident request-level routing logs, map of KMS key usage, and a 90-day audit log export. Compliance will require a 2-week pre-prod canary and compliance sign-off.
4) Timeline and next steps: Engineering will scope and deliver the routing flag + guardrails in 2 sprints once the Dedicated capacity order is placed; infra provisioning may add additional lead time. Legal/Sales should include the specific acceptance criteria and the capacity requirement in the contract.

Rishi: please communicate this back to Acme as our engineering position. I'll work with Evelyn to draft the compliance language and with Markus to produce the capacity estimates sheet for procurement.

If Acme requires an alternative (hosted w/soft-fallback), list that as a fallback commercial offering.

- Lauren
